topic_text: Topic 5.5: Basic EPS restated for a rights issue's bonus element using the theoretical ex-rights fair value adjustment factor
question_html: Following information is supplied by K Ltd.: Number of shares outstanding prior to right issue - 2,50,000 shares. Right issue - two new share for each 5 outstanding shares (i.e. 1,00,000 new shares). Right issue price - ₹98. Last date of exercising rights - 30-06-2023. Fair value of one equity share immediately prior to exercise of right on 30-06-2023 is ₹102. Net Profit to equity shareholders: 2022-2023 - ₹50,00,000; 2023-2024 - ₹75,00,000. You are required to calculate the basic earnings per share as per AS-20 Earnings per Share.
answer_html:
Theoretical ex-rights fair value per share = (Fair value of shares immediately prior to exercise of rights + Total amount received from exercise) / (Number of shares outstanding prior to exercise + Number of shares issued in the exercise) = (₹102 × 2,50,000 shares + ₹98 × 1,00,000 shares) / 3,50,000 shares = ₹100.86.

Computation of adjustment factor = Fair value per share prior to exercise of rights / Theoretical ex-rights value per share = 102/100.86 = 1.01.

Computation of earnings per share:

EPS for the year 2022-23 as originally reported: ₹50,00,000/2,50,000 shares = ₹20.

EPS for the year 2022-23 restated for rights issue: ₹50,00,000/(2,50,000 shares × 1.01) = ₹19.80.

EPS for the year 2023-24 including effects of rights issue: EPS = ₹75,00,000/3,25,625* = ₹23.03.

* [(2,50,000 × 1.01 × 3/12) + (3,50,000 × 9/12)] = 63,125 + 2,62,500 = 3,25,625 shares.

Note: Financial year (ended 31st March) is considered as accounting year while giving the above answer.
mistake_text: Author’s Note: A common error is using the raw share count and nominal rights-issue price directly, without first computing the theoretical ex-rights fair value and applying the resulting adjustment factor to the pre-rights weighted average.

topic_text: Topic 5.6: Diluted EPS from convertible debentures, with partly-paid shares weighted by proportion paid
question_html: On 1st April, 2025, ABC Limited: 50,000 equity shares of ₹100 each (₹80 paid up by all shareholders) ₹40,00,000; 2,00,000 8% Preference shares of ₹10 each ₹20,00,000; 10,000 12% Debentures of ₹100 each (each convertible into 3 equity shares of ₹100 each) ₹10,00,000. On 1st July 2025, remaining ₹20 called up and paid by all shareholders except one holding 10,000 equity shares. Profit after tax for 2025-26: ₹3,44,000. Tax rate 30%. Compute Basic and Diluted EPS.
answer_html:
Basic EPS: Net profit attributable to equity = 3,44,000 − preference dividend (8% × 20,00,000 = 1,60,000) = 1,84,000. Weighted average equity shares: 1 Apr–30 Jun (50,000 shares × 80/100 paid × 3/12) = 10,000 + 1 Jul–31 Mar (40,000 fully-paid shares × 9/12) = 30,000 + (10,000 shares still ₹80-paid × 80/100 × 9/12) = 6,000; total = 46,000. Basic EPS = 1,84,000 / 46,000 = ₹4 per share.

Diluted EPS: Interest on 10,000 12% debentures = 1,20,000; tax relief @30% = 36,000; net interest add-back = 84,000. Adjusted net profit = 1,84,000 + 1,20,000 − 36,000 = 2,68,000. Shares from conversion (10,000 debentures × 3) = 30,000. Diluted shares = 46,000 + 30,000 = 76,000. Diluted EPS = 2,68,000 / 76,000 = ₹3.53 per share (approx).
mistake_text: Author’s Note: Some examinees forgot to add back the after-tax interest saving on the convertible debentures to net profit when computing diluted EPS, or omitted weighting the partly-paid shares by the proportion actually paid up.

topic_text: Topic 5.3: Weighted average number of shares - the effective date to use for shares issued under six different circumstances
question_html:
In the following list of shares issued, for the purpose of calculation of weighted average number of shares, from which date, weight is to be considered:

  1. Equity Shares issued in exchange of cash,
  2. Equity Shares issued as a result of conversion of a debt instrument,
  3. Equity Shares issued in exchange for the settlement of a liability of the enterprise,
  4. Equity Shares issued for rendering of services to the enterprise,
  5. Equity Shares issued in lieu of interest and/or principal of an other financial instrument,
  6. Equity Shares issued as consideration for the acquisition of an asset other than in cash.
answer_html:
The following dates should be considered for weights for the purpose of calculation of weighted average number of shares in the given situations:

  1. Date of Cash receivable
  2. Date of conversion
  3. Date on which settlement becomes effective
  4. When the services are rendered
  5. Date when interest ceases to accrue
  6. Date on which the acquisition is recognised.
mistake_text: Author’s Note: A common error is defaulting to "date of allotment" for every scenario, without distinguishing situations where AS 20 specifies a different effective date, e.g. shares issued in lieu of interest are weighted from when interest ceases to accrue, not the allotment date.

topic_text: Topic 5.4: Inclusion-date rules for shares issued under various circumstances, for weighted average share count
question_html: In the following list of shares issued, for the purpose of calculation of weighted average number of shares, from which date, weight is to be considered: (i) Equity Shares issued in exchange of cash, (ii) Equity Shares issued as a result of conversion of a debt instrument, (iii) Equity Shares issued in exchange for the settlement of a liability of the enterprise, (iv) Equity Shares issued for rendering of services to the enterprise, (v) Equity Shares issued in lieu of interest and/or principal of an other financial instrument, (vi) Equity Shares issued as consideration for the acquisition of an asset other than in cash. (5 Marks)
answer_html: (i) Date of Cash receivable. (ii) Date of conversion. (iii) Date on which settlement becomes effective. (iv) When the services are rendered. (v) Date when interest ceases to accrue. (vi) Date on which the acquisition is recognised.
mistake_text: Author’s Note: Many examinees used the date of the board resolution or agreement for several of these cases instead of the specific triggering event AS 20 identifies (e.g. date of conversion, date services are rendered), inflating or understating the weighted average share count.

topic_text: Topic 5.5: Rights issue with a bonus element - theoretical ex-rights value, adjustment factor, and restatement of the comparative year's EPS
question_html:
From the financial records of P Limited: Profit before tax FY2023-24 ₹25,00,000; FY2024-25 ₹32,50,000. Number of Equity Shares (Face Value ₹5) outstanding as on 31st March, 2024: 12,00,000. Applicable Tax Rate for both years: 20%. On 1st June, 2024, Directors announced a rights issue: 1 share for every 6 held @ ₹20/share, exercisable to 30th June, 2024, fully subscribed. Fair value of one equity share immediately prior to exercise of right (30th June, 2024) was ₹25.

You are required to calculate the Basic Earnings per Share to be reported in the financial statements of P Limited for the year ended 31st March, 2025, including the comparative figure for the year ended 31st March, 2024, in accordance with AS 20. (5 Marks)
answer_html:
Computation of Basic Earnings Per Share (as per paragraphs 10 and 26 of AS 20):

Working Note 1 – Net Profit after tax (NPAT): 2024 = 25,00,000 − 20% tax = ₹20,00,000. 2025 = 32,50,000 − 20% tax = ₹26,00,000.

Working Note 2 – Theoretical ex-rights fair value per share: (Fair value of all outstanding shares immediately prior to rights + Total received from exercise) / (Shares outstanding prior + Shares issued in exercise) = (25×12,00,000 + 20×2,00,000) / (12,00,000+2,00,000) = 3,40,00,000/14,00,000 = ₹24.29.

Working Note 3 – Adjustment factor: Fair value per share prior to exercise / Theoretical ex-rights value = 25/24.29 = 1.029 (approx.).

ParticularsYear 2024 (₹)Year 2025 (₹)
EPS for the year 2024 as originally reported (20,00,000/12,00,000 shares)1.67
EPS for the year 2024 restated for rights issue [20,00,000/(12,00,000×1.029)] = 20,00,000/12,35,2801.62 (approx.)
EPS for the year 2025 including effects of rights issue: 26,00,000 / [(12,00,000×1.029×3/12)+(14,00,000×9/12)] = 26,00,000/13,58,700 shares1.91 (approx.)
mistake_text: Examiner’s Comment: Many examinees were unable to compute Earnings Per Share correctly in accordance with AS 20 "Earnings Per Share." A common error was the use of profit before tax instead of profit after tax for EPS calculation. Additionally, some examinees failed to determine the correct number of equity shares for computation. Mistakes were also observed in calculating profit after tax, the weighted average number of shares, and the bonus element in rights issues.

topic_text: Topic 5.9: Anti-dilutive potential equity shares (those that would decrease loss per share) are excluded from diluted EPS
question_html:
XYZ Limited has a wholly owned subsidiary BC Limited. The Group prepares consolidated Financial Statements for the year ended 31st March, 2024. XYZ Limited (in its separate financial statements) has incurred a loss of ₹2 crore during the year, while the consolidated profit for the group during the year is ₹40 lakh.

XYZ Limited has 5,00,000 shares outstanding as at 31st March, 2024. Further, it has granted options to issue equity shares as at that date. In respect of such options, 1,00,000 shares are considered to be the shares issued for no consideration. There are no changes in income or expenses that are expected from the issue of equity shares on exercise of these options.

Calculate Basic and Diluted EPS for XYZ Limited for separate financial statements and for the Group.
answer_html:
Computation of earnings per share

ParticularsConsolidated financial statementsStandalone financial statements of XYZ Limited
Basic earnings/(loss) per share₹8 [40,00,000/5,00,000](₹40) [2,00,00,000/5,00,000]
Diluted earnings/(loss) per share₹6.66 [40,00,000/6,00,000](₹40) [2,00,00,000/5,00,000]

As per paragraph 39 of AS 20, "Potential equity shares should be treated as dilutive when, and only when, their conversion to equity shares would decrease net profit per share from continuing ordinary operations."

In the above case, if the exercise of options was considered for the separate financial statements of XYZ Limited, the diluted loss per share would have reduced to ₹33.33 [2,00,00,000/6,00,000]. As this is anti-dilutive, the options would not be treated as potentially dilutive equity shares. Accordingly, in the separate financial statements of XYZ Limited, the Diluted EPS would be the same as Basic EPS.
mistake_text: Author’s Note: A common error is including the anti-dilutive effect of the share options in the standalone diluted EPS computation because it appears to reduce the reported loss per share, missing that AS 20 requires potential equity shares to be excluded from diluted EPS whenever their inclusion would be anti-dilutive from the standpoint of continuing ordinary operations.

topic_text: Topic 5.2: Mandatory-reserve appropriations remain attributable to equity shareholders and are not excluded from the EPS numerator
question_html: Should appropriation to mandatory reserves be excluded from net profit attributable to equity shareholders? AB Limited must, per an agreement with debenture holders, appropriate profits each year to a specific reserve such that, at redemption, the reserve equals at least half the debenture value. Since these appropriations aren't available for distribution to equity shareholders, AB Limited excluded them from the Basic EPS numerator. Is this correct?
answer_html:
The appropriation to such a mandatory reserve should be included in net profit attributable to equity shareholders for computing Basic EPS — AB Limited's treatment is not correct.

AS 20 para 11 defines the numerator as net profit/loss for the period "attributable to equity shareholders" — after deducting preference dividends and attributable tax, but nothing else. Emphasis on "attributable to equity shareholders" (not "available for distribution") means amounts appropriated to mandatory reserves, though not distributable as dividend, remain attributable to equity shareholders in substance (the reserve still belongs to them, merely earmarked). They should therefore be included in the Basic EPS computation.
mistake_text: Author’s Note: Some examinees conflated "attributable to equity shareholders" with "distributable to equity shareholders," incorrectly excluding non-distributable mandatory-reserve appropriations from the EPS numerator.

topic_text: Topic 5.6-5.8: Diluted EPS: numerator add-back of post-tax interest on dilutive convertible debentures, denominator inclusion of shares issuable on conversion
question_html:
The following information relates to XYZ Limited for the year ended 31st March, 2024: Net Profit for the year after tax: ₹37,50,000. Number of Equity Shares of ₹10 each outstanding: 5,00,000. Convertible Debentures issued by the Company (at the beginning of the year):

ParticularsNos.
8% Convertible Debentures of ₹100 each50,000
Equity Shares to be issued on conversion55,000

The Rate of Income Tax: 30%. You are required to calculate Basic and Diluted Earnings Per Share (EPS).
answer_html:
Basic EPS = Net profit for the current year / Weighted average number of equity shares outstanding = ₹37,50,000 / 5,00,000 = ₹7.50 per share.

Diluted EPS = Adjusted net profit for the current year / Weighted average number of equity shares (including dilutive potential equity shares):

Adjusted net profit for the current year₹
Net profit for the current year37,50,000
Add: Interest expense for the current year (8% × ₹50,00,000 face value)4,00,000
Less: Tax relating to interest expense (30% of ₹4,00,000)(1,20,000)
Adjusted net profit for the current year40,30,000

Number of equity shares resulting from conversion of debentures = 55,000 (given in the question). Weighted average number of equity shares for diluted EPS = 5,00,000 + 55,000 = 5,55,000 shares.

Diluted EPS = ₹40,30,000 / 5,55,000 = ₹7.26 per share.

Note: Conversion of the convertible debentures into equity shares is a dilutive potential equity share. To compute the adjusted profit, the (post-tax) interest paid on the debentures is added back, since it would not be payable if the debentures were converted into equity shares.
mistake_text: Author’s Note: A common error is adding back the full pre-tax interest expense to the numerator without deducting the related tax effect, overstating the adjusted net profit used for diluted EPS.

topic_text: Topic 5.5: Rights issue EPS restatement using the theoretical ex-rights fair value adjustment factor
question_html:
The following information is available in respect of High-end Ltd. for the accounting year 2022-2023 and 2023-2024:

Net profit for₹
Year2022-202322,00,000
Year2023-202430,00,000

Number of shares outstanding prior to right issue 10,00,000 shares.

Right issue: One new share for each five shares outstanding i.e. 2,00,000 shares.

: Right issue price ₹25

: Last date to exercise right 31st July, 2023.

Fair value of one equity share immediately prior to exercise of rights on 31.07.2023 is ₹32.

You are required to compute, as per AS 20:

  1. Basic earnings per share for the year 2022-2023.
  2. Restated basic earnings per share for the year 2022-20223 for right issue.
  3. Basic earnings per share for the year 2023-2024.
answer_html:
Computation of basic earnings per share

2022-2023 (₹)2023-2024 (₹)
EPS for the year 2022-2023 as originally reported = Net profit for the year attributable to equity shareholders / weighted average number of equity shares outstanding during the year = ₹22,00,000 / 10,00,000 shares2.20
EPS for the year 2022-2023 restated for the right issue = ₹22,00,000 / (10,00,000 × 1.04)2.12
EPS for the year 2023-2024 (including effect of right issue) = ₹30,00,000 / {(10,00,000 × 1.04 × 4/12) + (12,00,000 × 8/12)}2.62

Working Notes:

  1. Computation of theoretical ex-rights fair value per share = (fair value of all outstanding shares immediately prior to exercise of rights + Total value received from exercise of rights) / (number of shares outstanding prior to exercise + number of shares issued on the exercise)
    = (₹32 × 10,00,000 + ₹25 × 2,00,000) / (10,00,000 + 2,00,000)
    = ₹30.83
  2. Computation of adjustment factor
    = Fair value per share prior to exercise of rights / Theoretical ex-right value per share
    = ₹32/₹30.83
    = 1.04 (approx.)
mistake_text: Author’s Note: A common error is applying the rights-issue adjustment factor only to the current year's weighted average share count and forgetting to restate the prior year's (2022-2023) EPS by the same factor for comparability.
